Ronja kept creating, not despite it all, but because of it. In her talk “The Surprising Power of Negative Thinking,” she reveals how the same tools that helped her grow a business became tools for navigating her diagnosis and how they can help you, too. Ronja believes: “Entrepreneurship isn’t just for companies: It’s for everyday life.”

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Fix your face. Dr Ralph Hughes reveals how perception shapes identity, judgment, and the way we misunderstand each other.
Have you ever been misjudged before anyone truly knew you?
In this insightful TEDx talk, Dr Ralph Hughes shares powerful stories from his childhood in Harlem to his career in federal law enforcement, showing how quickly people form assumptions without context. From a child protecting his ice cream on a stoop to being labeled “guarded” or “better than others,” he exposes how perception often replaces truth.
Dr Hughes introduces a simple but powerful framework: Stop, Caution, Go. A mental “traffic light” that helps us pause judgment, become aware of bias, and move forward with curiosity and empathy instead of assumption.
This talk challenges how we label others and how easily those labels can become identity if left unchecked.
Watch and reflect: are you seeing people as they are, or as you assume them to be?
perception and identity, Dr Ralph Hughes TEDx, unconscious
title: Fix your face: The danger of personality perception | Dr Ralph J. Hughes | TEDxMiramar

description:
In a world that often feels divided, Chandni Dhingra invites us to reflect on the strength of shared experience and the journey of finding where we truly belong.

Through her talk, Chandni explores the power of community, identity, and self-awareness — drawing from her experiences and her work in social change movements. She shows how understanding ourselves more deeply can lead us to the people who uplift, challenge, and stand with us.
 Chandni Dhingra is a Policy Adviser at the ICRC working on both policy and UN diplomacy. She has experience at the intersection of humanitarian action, human rights and development, and has a background in legal practice. Her previous work has focused on displacement, child protection, gender, and transitional justice, including in East Africa, South East Asia, and Australia. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

description:
We’ve been told that planting trees is our best shot at fighting the climate crisis. But what if we’ve been looking at the wrong ecosystem?

In this eye-opening talk, Ann Christin Kornelsen, founder of the NGO Mission to Marsh, reveals the silent superpower beneath our feet: peatlands. Despite covering only 3% of the Earth’s surface, these forgotten 'wastelands' store twice as much carbon as all the world’s forests combined. While we have overlooked the power of peatlands for centuries, the time has come to open our eyes and see how they can protect us.
 Ann Christin Kornelsen is a geographer, climate advocate, and the founder of the award-winning NGO Mission to Marsh. She leverages a broad global network to research and protect wetlands, transforming scientific data into actionable conservation efforts to preserve the Earth's most critical carbon sinks.

description:
We are the most connected generation in history, but does that mean we are the best informed? Or are we the most clueless? In this powerful TEDx talk, Michael Kaufmann, Head of Digital at Medienhaus Wimmer, a well-known media company in Austria, reveals how Big Tech's attention algorithms are not bringing us closer together. Instead, they are leaving us in "news deserts", where democracy dies in darkness. Learn why your screen time is a problem and what you can personally do to protect truth as a public resource.

This talk is a must-watch for anyone who wants to understand how the attention economy is changing our public conversation. It explores how Big Tech is redefining the journalism landscape and the way social media algorithms influence our shared reality. A wake-up call for media literacy and a guide on how we, as informed citizens, can protect democracy.
 Michael Kaufmann is a digital enthusiast who has spent over a decade examining the technical and economic sides of the med
title: How Social Media Undermines Democracy | Michael Kaufmann | TEDxLinz

description:
Trigger warning: This content contains discussions of suicide.

What remains of the people we love after they are gone? In this deeply personal TEDx talk, Matthias Rettenbacher shares the story of losing his father at just 19 years old after his father disappeared during a battle with depression. The search that followed changed how he understands grief, family, and the invisible ways our parents continue to shape who we are.

Through memories of long drives, family struggles, and the moment he found his father in the forest, Matthias reflects on the complicated reality of love and loss. Over time, he began to notice something unexpected: pieces of his father still living on, in gestures, habits, and even in the smiles of his own sons.

This talk is a reflection on grief, legacy, and the courage it takes to break the cycles we inherit, so that the next generation can live more freely.
 Matthias Rettenbacher is an entrepreneur, storyteller, and father who believes that the stories we i
title: What My Father’s Death Taught Me About Life | Matthias Rettenbacher | TEDxLinz

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Have you ever considered the relationship between production and place, and what it means for cities to truly sustain themselves? Drawing on the Fab City model's radical shift from PITO (Products In, Trash Out) to DIDO (Data In, Data Out), Kate asks a deceptively simple question: what would it mean to produce locally again?

Drawing on firsthand experience from urban and regional experiments around the world, Kate shows us how makers and community members in Bali, Indonesia, are harnessing technology to harvest blue hydrogen, and to Hamburg, where open source mid-scale manufacturing facilities are putting the means of production back in the hands of citizens. This talk reveals how technology, when placed in the hands of communities, can close the loop between a place and what sustains it, building something more connected, more resilient, and more human.
 Join Kate on this journey into the cities and systems that could sustain us. Kate is a context architect, CEO of the Fab City Found
title: Redesigning Production and Place: Can Technology Reconnect Us? | Kate Armstrong | TEDxLinz

This connection also inspires a sense of responsibility to protect and live sustainably with nature. Dr. Vijaya Bharat, a cardiology consultant in Jamshedpur, graduated from Medical College Trivandrum, Kerala, and joined Tata Main Hospital (TMH) in 1977. Beginning with a simple yet powerful idea, the demand curve, he explores how economics reveals patterns beneath apparent chaos, offering a lens to understand how individuals and markets function.

Building on decades of research, he questions a foundational assumption: that individuals act purely in their own self-interest. While this idea has driven innovation and growth, he examines its limitations in addressing some of today’s most pressing global challenges, from inequality to climate change.

Introducing the concept of identity as the core driver of decision-making, Pawan reframes the way we think about “self.” Through a compelling metaphor of a wave and the ocean, he illustrates how individuals are both independent and deeply interconnected. Tayten introduces the idea of “silent leadership” and explains how your attitude, discipline, and choices shape the people around you whether you realize it or not. Xavier Murphy, a speaker on family systems and identity, shares a deeply personal Christmas dinner moment that exposes how hidden truths don’t disappear, they reshape families, roles, and relationships across decades.
This TEDx talk challenges how we think about truth, loyalty, and protection within families. You will walk away understanding how unspoken stories affect self-perception and why silence often does more damage than disclosure.
Watch this if you have ever questioned your family history, felt misplaced in your identity, or sensed there is a story beneath the surface that was never told. Watch fully, reflect on your own family narratives, and consider what silence may still be shaping your life today.

He explores how these unspoken pressures shape the way we think, act, and connect with others, often pushing us into silence.

Through relatable insights, he highlights how many people hide their true feelings to fit expectations, avoid criticism, or protect their image. But at what cost? author: TEDx Talks
description:
Dr. Tara Rajendran, MBBS, Ph.D., MFA, presents a captivating classical South Indian Saraswati Veena recital in the Raga (musical mode) Amritavarshini (‘the shower of nectar’), an evocative melodic framework long associated with rain.

The performance opens with a graceful elaboration of the raga, introducing the distinct gait. This leads into the meditative and nuanced ‘Taana’, a dynamic rhythmic–melodic improvisatory passage in which the Raga is explored through inventive permutations across notes and strings with controlled transitions in pace and rhythm. The recital then proceeds to the composition “Sudhamayi Sudhanidhe”, in Sanskrit by Harikeshanallur Muthiah Bhagavatar, set in Rupaka tala. The ‘Kriti’ praises the Goddess ‘Vijayambika’. And it includes a brief ‘Niraval,’ where a chosen phrase becomes the ground for imaginative improvisations within the framework of the composition.

Dr. Rajendran began her traditional Veena training at the age of seven and was a disciple of Venkit

Through real-world cases and neuroscience research, I reveal how habits, thoughts, and deliberate practice physically reshape our neural pathways. Neuroplasticity shows that change is not merely motivational language, but a biological reality. When we recognize that our brains are constantly adapting, we begin to understand that who we become is not predetermined but continuously shaped by what we repeatedly choose to do. Hi everyone! author: TEDx Talks
description:
When we witness injustice, we are told that "awareness" is the first step toward change. But what happens when everyone is aware, yet nothing moves? Drawing from her journey—from a 15-year-old witnessing the collapse of carriage horses in Florence to her current work at the intersection of international law, space technology, and aviation—Tuana Yazici argues that empathy alone is a fragile foundation for progress.
In this compelling talk, Yazici reveals why the most persistent "blind spots" in our most advanced technologies—from AI algorithms to satellite systems—are actually design choices. She challenges us to move beyond "caring louder" and instead start embedding accountability into the very architecture of our future. If our sense of responsibility doesn't scale as fast as our creations, our greatest innovations risk becoming nothing more than velocity without direction. Tuana Yazici is a licensed attorney in Florida, and the Founder, Chair, and CEO of the holding company Tuana G
title: Caring Is Not Enough: Why Responsibility Must Be Designed | Tuana Yazici | TEDxSaintAndrewsSchool

Sustainability is no longer just about protecting the environment. It is about redesigning the systems that shape our future.

In this TEDx talk, Atun Roy explores how sustainability has evolved from a moral responsibility into a powerful design principle, one that now determines how we build, innovate, and grow. What was once seen as a constraint is now becoming the foundation of smarter systems, stronger businesses, and more resilient ideas.

Through a compelling personal story from his work in waste innovation, Atun shares how a failed “sustainable” system led to a deeper realization. The real challenge was never waste itself, but the way we designed around it. That shift in thinking became the foundation for reimagining waste not as a burden, but as a resource.

description:
A TEDx talk by Rita Mendonca on Maun Vrat, the ancient Indian practice of intentional silence, reimagined through the lens of modern psychology, neuroscience, and lived experience. Blending traditional wisdom, contemporary brain science, and a deeply personal story about her nani, Rita explores silence not as absence, but as a form of mental discipline.
From emotional regulation and neuroplasticity to overstimulation and cognitive overload, this talk reveals how silence can help reduce internal noise, restore clarity, and build the kind of steadiness we often mistake for strength. In a world shaped by constant notifications, endless input, and mental fatigue, Maun Vrat is no longer just a spiritual ritual. It is a practical tool for psychological resilience. Dr. Rita Mendonca is the founder of My Mind Gains, a psychologist and therapist known for making mental health conversations accessible and engaging. title: Maun Vrat: The Subtle Art of Just Being | Rita Mendonca | TEDxVITBhopal

description: How many transgender people do you have to know to be an ally? Only one. In this talk, George Johnson shares his personal story of growing up transgender and his luck in getting life-saving treatment just two weeks before it was banned in his state. He shares the fear, love, and general discomfort of puberty at 17 so that everyone can meet a trans person and learn how to let trans kids grow up. George Johnson is a college freshman studying political science and human rights. He came out as transgender at 10 years old and has been living his true life as a male since. Having been given access to gender affirming care in his teens, closely before it was banned in his state, he aims to protect other young trans people through activism and telling his story with public speaking. Along with giving speeches, George gives 1-on-1 coaching to Speech and Debate students across the country. He is studying human rights to become a politician dedicated to helping marginalized groups. Loza's talk explores how true progress is rooted in the power of mutual understanding and the willingness to engage with opposing ideas. Her interest in the art of discourse began with a simple habit: watching online debates to better understand perspectives vastly different from her own. Through this, she realized that while total agreement isn't always possible, the empathy to listen is the only real engine for social change.
